battle.name: 竇建德兼併魏刀兒之戰
battle.theater: 河北南部洺州魏郡一帶
battle.brief: 大業十三年（617），河北起兵首領竇建德與同郡的魏刀兒由並肩轉為相攻，竇建德在河北南部擊破魏刀兒之眾，併其兵眾與城池，自此河北只剩他一家勢力，為兩年後唐軍洺水之戰埋下伏線。卡面科林斯青銅盔雖非戰場之物，其「靠隊形活」的邏輯，正是這批以方陣自保的起兵眾的真實寫照。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 交戰的一方是竇建德率領的河北起兵眾。竇建德出身河北鄉里的農戶，父竇孝騫在隋朝任郡丞，他募兵自保，聚眾數千，漸為郡縣殘兵與流亡農民所歸附，一度與同在河北的魏刀兒、高開道等群雄並立；其下多為鄉兵與渠帥所領的散眾，器械雜用，沒有統一的編制與糧秣制度。另一方是魏刀兒的起兵眾。魏刀兒同樣出自河北民間，以「魏」為號，聚眾數萬，據河北南部魏郡、洺州一帶的鄉里與山寨，組織鬆散，糧食多靠就地徵斂，沒有穩定的屯田與後勤基地。兩軍最初並非死敵：河北大亂之際，各方互相援引，竇建德與魏刀兒分兵合勢、互為犄角，局勢一緊，才各自打起吞併對方的主意。背景中還有兩股力量必須交代：其一是隋朝的地方官軍，郡兵在隋末已多崩潰倒戈，調往河北的援軍往往未至而先散，隋廷對起兵者時而羈縻授官、時而發兵討平，實際上已無法再統合河北；其二是次年在長安建立的唐朝，李淵以關中為根本，遣使招撫河北群雄，竇建德與魏刀兒都在這盤棋的招撫與討伐名單之上。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the Hebei rebel host led by Dou Jiande and the rebel host of Wei Dao'er. Dou Jiande came out of a farming family in the Hebei countryside; his father Dou Xiaolian served as a commandery deputy under the Sui, and Dou raised troops to protect his own locality, gathering several thousand men who were gradually joined by the remnants of commandery garrisons and by peasants who had fled their homes. For a time he stood on a par with the other Hebei strongmen such as Wei Dao'er and Gao Kaidao; the troops under him were mostly village levies and bands led by local strongmen, with mixed equipment and no unified system of organisation or supply. The other side was Wei Dao'er's rebel host. Wei too came out of the common people of Hebei, took the character Wei as his banner, gathered tens of thousands of men and occupied the villages and stockaded strongholds around Wei Commandery and Ming Prefecture in southern Hebei; his organisation was loose, his food was taken largely by local requisition, and he had no settled land under cultivation and no stable logistical base. The two hosts were not at first mortal enemies: in the general disorder in Hebei every group relied on the others, and Dou Jiande and Wei Dao'er joined forces and covered each other's flanks until the situation tightened, and only then did each begin to plot the swallowing of the other. Two further forces have to be taken into account. The first was the Sui's local government troops: by the end of the dynasty the commandery levies had largely collapsed or defected, and reinforcements sent to Hebei often dispersed before they even arrived; the Sui court, alternately offering titles to the insurgents and dispatching armies to put them down, could no longer really hold Hebei together. The second was the Tang dynasty, founded the following year at Chang'an; Li Yuan took Guanzhong as his base and sent envoys to pacify the Hebei strongmen, and both Dou Jiande and Wei Dao'er stood on the list of those to be won over or destroyed.
people: 核心人物是竇建德。史傳他起兵之後以信義相結，重用河北舊吏與鄉兵渠帥，作戰先設陣而後進，屢以合圍與突騎制勝。兼併魏刀兒時，他並未選擇與對手硬拼到底，而是先斷其外援、孤立其眾，再以主力一次擊破，把對方的兵眾與城池一併收編，使自己的規模在數月之間膨脹數倍，這是河北群雄中最見效率的一次擴張。魏刀兒本人是河北較早起事者之一，靠聚眾與據守鄉里打開局面，在竇建德勢力坐大之前，兩人幾可平分河北；但他未能整合旗下各部，也沒有穩固的根據地，一旦首戰受挫，部眾便各自星散，其本人下落諸史記載互有出入，一說戰歿於陣，一說為部下所殺，一說脫身後不知所在。與他們同期在河北舉事的還有張金稱與高士達：一般認為張金稱其後為竇建德所破，高士達北走幽州依託高開道——三人的分合說明河北起兵群並非鐵板一塊，而是隨強弱消長不斷重組。隋朝一方能確認的，只是奉命討伐河北的將領與郡兵；唐初的樞紐則是李淵、李世民父子，李世民的介入最終改寫了河北的歸屬。
peopleEn: The central figure is Dou Jiande. The histories record that after raising his troops he bound men to him by trust and good faith, employed the old officials of Hebei together with the village leaders of the local levies, and in battle always formed up before he advanced, winning again and again by encirclement and by cavalry strikes. When he took over Wei Dao'er he did not choose to grind the opponent down in a straight fight; he cut off the enemy's external support and isolated his followers, then broke him in one decisive stroke with his main force, absorbing the enemy soldiers and the enemy cities at a single time, so that his own strength swelled severalfold within a few months — the most efficient single expansion among the Hebei strongmen. Wei Dao'er himself was one of the earlier risers in Hebei, opening his position by gathering followers and holding the countryside; before Dou Jiande grew large the two men could more or less divide Hebei between them. But Wei never managed to weld his various bands together and had no firm base, so once he was checked in his first engagement his men scattered in every direction, and his own fate is given in conflicting accounts: some say he died in the battle, some that his own men killed him, others that he escaped and was never heard from again. Two other men who rose in Hebei at the same time were Zhang Jincheng and Gao Shida; it is generally held that Zhang was later broken by Dou Jiande and that Gao Shida withdrew north to Youzhou to take shelter with Gao Kaidao. The way these three men separated and converged shows that the Hebei insurgents were never a single block but a field constantly recombining according to the waxing and waning of strength. On the Sui side all that can be confirmed is the generals and the commandery levies sent to campaign in Hebei; in the new Tang the pivot was the father and son Li Yuan and Li Shimin, and Li Shimin's intervention in the end decided to whom Hebei would belong.
kits: 卡面這具科林斯青銅盔，公元前七世紀中葉定型，是希臘重裝步兵的頭部防具：整盔覆面，只留一道縱向鼻脊與兩側眼孔，頸部靠一圈寬闊護頸與肩甲相接；代價是視野極窄、散熱難行，戴者幾乎放棄了用眼睛找目標的可能，只能靠同伴的旗幟、號角與身側的人牆行動——這正是「看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活」的來處。公元六百一十七年的河北戰場上當然沒有這件希臘器物，隋軍的對應裝備是兜鍪配護項與面甲的組合：披膊掩住上臂與頸側，銅葉或鐵葉面甲只露口鼻一線，明光鎧的護胸在日光下反光，藉以在亂陣中維持辨識；步卒以長矛列陣，騎兵用馬槊與直刀，弓弩交射在兩翼展開。竇建德這支部眾的裝備則明顯簡陋：成員多為農民與鄉兵，皮甲、布甲居多，頭部防護以舊氈布纏為主，能湊齊制式兜鍪者有限，因此更依賴長矛密集的方陣與衝撞，而不是個人甲冑的防護力。也正因如此，把科林斯青銅盔放上這張卡，講的正是同一個道理：頭盔保護得越好，隊形就越成為唯一的依靠。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card was fixed in form in the middle of the seventh century BC and was the head protection of the Greek heavy infantry: the whole helm covers the face, leaving only a vertical nasal ridge and an opening at each eye, and the neck is closed by a broad flange that meets the shoulder piece. The price is an extremely narrow field of view and poor ventilation; the man wearing it practically gave up finding his target with his eyes and could only act on the standards, the horns and the wall of men at his side. That is where the card's line comes from: the visible cost of the helmet is that the man who wears it can only live by the formation. There was of course no such Greek piece on the field in Hebei in AD 617. The Sui equivalent was the combination of a helmet with a neck guard and a face mask: shoulder flaps covered the upper arm and the side of the neck, bronze or iron face plates left only the mouth and nose in a slit, and the gleaming front plates of the bright armour reflected the sunlight so that a man could still be picked out in a mêlée. Infantry fought in spear ranks, cavalry carried cavalry lances and straight sabres, and bow and crossbow fire was opened up on the flanks. The equipment of Dou Jiande's host was markedly poorer: most of his men were peasants and village levies in leather or cloth armour, their heads protected mostly by old felt and cloth wrappings, and few could be issued regulation helmets. They therefore leaned far more on the density of the spear ranks and on the charge than on the protection of individual armour. That is exactly why a Corinthian helmet belongs on this card: the better the helmet protects you, the more the formation becomes your only support.
tactics: 這場兼併的戰術細節，諸史留下的文字極少，只能從隋末唐初河北作戰的通例與竇建德本人的用兵習慣推想其大概。竇建德起兵後賴以成名的做法有三：一是合縱連橫，先與同在河北的起兵者分兵合勢，把散兵游勇聚成可以與官軍對抗的集團；二是避實擊虛，避開郡兵與城防完整的縣城，專在鄉里、山寨之間轉戰；三是步兵結陣、騎兵繞擊，每逢大戰先以步卒列陣牽制對手，再遣騎兵迂迴其側後與糧道。兼併魏刀兒時，他大致沿用同一套路：先以遊騎封住對方往北、往西的通道，切斷其與高開道等河北勢力的聯繫，使魏刀兒只剩孤軍；然後集中兵力攻其外圍據點與部眾聚落，逼其離開熟悉的鄉里地盤；待對方陣腳一亂即乘勢併入其眾，隨即以受降者補自己的兵源與糧秣，加厚方陣。兩軍接觸多在平原會戰與村落攻奪之間轉換，河北平原適合車馬縱橫而少有山險可恃，決定勝負的往往是糧道與士氣而非城牆。卡面這具科林斯青銅盔在此點出關鍵：全覆的頭盔把人封在自己的世界裡，隊形與傳令就是眼睛的替代品；竇建德的眾多兵同樣如此，方陣越密，個人視野越小，勝敗越取決於號令能否貫穿全隊。
tacticsEn: Almost nothing is recorded about the tactical detail of this takeover, so it can only be reconstructed in outline from the general practice of campaigning in Hebei at the end of the Sui and from Dou Jiande's own habits. Three things made his name after he raised his troops. First, he worked through alliances: he joined forces with the other insurgents in Hebei, gathering scattered fighters into a group that could stand against the government troops. Second, he avoided strongpoints: he left alone the commandery garrisons and the counties with intact walls, and fought instead among the villages and the hill stockades. Third, he paired infantry formations with cavalry envelopment: in every major battle the foot closed ranks to hold the enemy, and then cavalry was sent round the flank and at the enemy's supply line. In taking over Wei Dao'er he followed much the same pattern. He first used light horse to seal the roads north and west, cutting Wei off from the other Hebei powers such as Gao Kaidao and leaving him an isolated army; then he concentrated his strength against the outer posts and the clusters of settlements where Wei's followers lived, driving him off the ground he knew; and as soon as that line began to break he moved in and took the men over, using the surrendered to fill his own ranks and provisions and to thicken his formations. Contact between the two sides passed back and forth between pitched battles on the plain and the assault on villages; the Hebei plain allowed cavalry and wagons to range widely while offering little in the way of broken ground, so what decided such a fight was usually the supply line and the state of the soldiers' morale rather than any wall. The Corinthian helmet on the card makes the point exactly: a fully enclosing helmet shuts a man inside his own small world, and the formation and the signals take the place of his eyes. Dou Jiande's multitude of men were the same in this respect — the denser the ranks, the smaller each man's view, and the more the outcome depended on whether the orders could be carried through the whole line.
data: 可核對的數字不多，先列確有根據的部分。竇建德生於公元五七三年，至這場兼併時約四十餘歲；公元六百一十七年對應隋煬帝大業十三年，唐要到次年才在長安建國。魏刀兒一軍的兵力，諸史多概稱眾數萬，並無確數；竇建德起兵初期所募為數千人，兼併魏刀兒並擊破張金稱之後，人數迅速增至數萬，到公元六百二十年前後，諸史稱其擁兵十餘萬、據有河北諸州，這些數目多為概數，不同史家記載相差頗大。地域上，戰事集中在河北南部的魏郡、洺州、冀州之間，離隋都洛陽不過數百里，離唐都長安則有一千五百里上下，通鑑與兩《唐書》常以離京師的里數標示這片區域的戰略價值。戰役確切的交戰日期與月份，諸史未詳記，本卡暫繫於大業十三年。能確定的因果鏈是清楚的：併掉魏刀兒與張金稱兩部之後，河北便只剩竇建德一家勢力，這正是兩年後唐軍在洺水以大軍擊潰夏軍的格局前提。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked, so let us set down the ones that have a basis. Dou Jiande was born in AD 573 and was a little over forty at the time of this takeover; AD 617 corresponds to the thirteenth year of the Daye era of Sui Emperor Yang, and the Tang would not be founded at Chang'an until the following year. The size of Wei Dao'er's host appears in the histories only in round figures, generally tens of thousands of men, with no exact count. Dou Jiande's own force at the outset was several thousand recruited men; after absorbing Wei Dao'er and breaking Zhang Jincheng his numbers rose rapidly into the tens of thousands, and by about AD 620 the histories say he had more than a hundred thousand men and held the prefectures of Hebei. These are approximations, and different historians differ considerably. Geographically the fighting was concentrated among Wei Commandery, Ming Prefecture and Ji Prefecture in southern Hebei, only a few hundred li from the Sui capital Luoyang and roughly fifteen hundred li from the Tang capital Chang'an; the Tongjian and the two Tang histories habitually marked the strategic value of this zone by the rough distances quoted from the capital. The exact day and month of the engagement are not recorded, and this card assigns it to the thirteenth year of Daye. What can be traced with certainty is the chain of cause and effect: once the bands of Wei Dao'er and Zhang Jincheng had been swallowed, only Dou Jiande's power was left in Hebei, and that was the precondition for the Tang army two years later to break the Xia army in massed battle at the Ming River.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最表層是河北實際控制權之爭：隋末郡縣體系崩解，河北土地肥沃、人丁稠密，饑荒、徭役與逃亡潮把大批農民推上道路，據城、掠糧、聚眾成了活下去的辦法；魏刀兒與竇建德都是這樣的起事者，兩軍同處河北一隅，起初因為各有敵人（官軍與旁支群雄）而互相容身，甚至同進同退，一旦一方坐大，另一方的生路便被堵死。第二層是竇建德自身的雄心：他並不滿足於做一名地方武裝的首領，而要吃掉河北，把散在各家的兵眾與城池收成自己的基業；對魏刀兒而言則是生存之爭——不是他想吞竇建德，而是他不吞竇建德，就會被竇建德吞掉，河北這塊地方容不下兩個這樣的人物。第三層是隋廷羈縻的失效：隋朝先後給起兵者授官封爵，希望以名分換服從，等到名分失去約束力，雙方便只剩兵戎相見；唐的出現則給了河北另一種選項——接受招撫而歸唐，或者被消滅。竇建德兼併魏刀兒，正是在這個轉折點上、在他要成為河北唯一主人之前，先把身邊的競爭者清掉。
causeEn: There are three layers of reason behind the fighting. The outermost is the struggle for actual control of Hebei: the commandery and county system of the Sui had come apart, Hebei had fertile land and a dense population, and famine, corvée labour and a tide of flight pushed large numbers of peasants onto the roads, where seizing a town, taking grain and raising a band had become a way to stay alive. Wei Dao'er and Dou Jiande were both risers of this kind; their two hosts stood in the same corner of Hebei and at first sheltered each other, even marching together, because each had enemies of his own — the government troops and the neighbouring strongmen — but as soon as one of them grew large the other found his way blocked. The second layer is Dou Jiande's own ambition: he was not content to remain the chief of a local armed band; he wanted to swallow Hebei and gather the scattered troops and cities into a base of his own. For Wei Dao'er it was a struggle for survival — not that he wished to devour Dou Jiande, but that unless he devoured Dou Jiande, he would be devoured in turn; Hebei had room for only one such figure. The third layer is the failure of the Sui court's method of control: the Sui first granted offices and titles to the insurgents in the hope of buying their submission with rank, and once rank had lost its force there was nothing left for the two sides but arms. The arrival of the Tang gave Hebei a further choice — accept the pacification and come over to the Tang, or be destroyed. Dou Jiande's absorption of Wei Dao'er came precisely at that turning point, before he became sole master of Hebei, when he first cleared the competitors around him.
impact: 對河北，這場兼併是一道分水嶺：兼併之前，河北起兵群大小首領並立，官軍尚能靠各打各的、各自平叛的辦法拖住局面；兼併之後，河北只剩竇建德一家，他有了足夠的兵眾與城池去與唐爭天下，有了足夠的錢糧去養兵、置官、建制，也有了足夠的勝利去吸引河北的士人與地方豪族歸心。對竇建德本人，這一步讓他從地方武裝首領變成割據一方的君主，其後進而稱帝、號夏，置州郡官屬、追尊祖考、郊天改元——這些都建立在河北整合完成的基礎上。對唐，這場兼併把北方的邊界問題變簡單了：李世民不必再逐個討伐河北群雄，只需在洺水一戰摧毀夏國骨幹，河北諸州便望風而降，唐朝於是把河北納入版圖，不必急著在北方用兵。對後世，這也說明隋末唐初的統一不是靠一次會戰完成，而是靠不斷兼併地方武裝、逐步收縮敵方空間的模式：先消化近處、壯大自己，最後才有條件與最強者正面決戰。
impactEn: For Hebei this takeover was a watershed. Before it, the Hebei insurgents were a field of big and small chiefs standing side by side, and the government troops could still hold things up by letting each rebel be defeated on his own; after it, only Dou Jiande's host was left in Hebei. He now had enough men and cities to contend with the Tang for the realm, enough money and grain to feed an army, appoint officials and build institutions, and enough victories to draw Hebei's scholars and local great families to his side. For Dou Jiande himself this step turned a leader of a local armed band into the ruler of a separatist state; he would later proclaim himself emperor of Xia, set up the officials of commanderies and prefectures, honour his ancestors as emperors, and perform the suburban sacrifice and change the era name — all of it resting on the completion of Hebei's unification. For the Tang the takeover simplified the northern problem: Li Shimin no longer had to defeat the Hebei strongmen one by one; a single battle at the Ming River shattered the backbone of Xia, the prefectures of Hebei came over, and the Tang took Hebei into its territory without having to fight a long northern war. For posterity it also shows that the unification of the late Sui and early Tang was not achieved in one set-piece battle but by a model of constantly absorbing local armed groups and steadily contracting the enemy's space: digest what is nearest first, grow strong, and only then be in a condition to meet the strongest opponent in open battle.
result: 結果是竇建德完勝。魏刀兒一軍在河北南部被擊潰，部眾被拆散、分編入竇建德的序列，一部分隨夏軍作戰，一部分解散返鄉；魏刀兒本人的下落諸史說法不一，無論戰歿、被部下所殺，還是出逃後隱沒，河北再沒有第二支能與竇建德抗衡的武裝。兼併之後，竇建德的兵勢在兩年之內膨脹到十餘萬人，佔有河北諸州，並於公元六百一十八年遣使奉表稱臣、受封夏王，其後進而稱帝，建立起一套以河北為根基的割據政權。公元六百二十一年十二月，秦王李世民在洺水大破夏軍，竇建德為部下所擒，押送長安，隨即被處斬，河北諸州相繼歸唐，河北重回中央王朝的版圖。回頭看，公元六百一十七年河北南部那場不見於詳戰記錄的兼併，正是這條結局的第一級台階：先兼併魏刀兒、張金稱等部眾而獨霸河北，再被唐軍在一次正面會戰中連根拔起，兩件事相距不足五年，中間只隔著一次洺水之戰。
resultEn: The result was an outright victory for Dou Jiande. Wei Dao'er's host was broken in southern Hebei, its men broken up and enrolled into Dou's ranks, some serving with the Xia army and some dispersed homeward. Wei's own fate is given differently in the histories; whether he fell in the fight, was killed by his own men, or escaped and vanished, Hebei never again had a second armed force able to stand against Dou Jiande. In the two years after the takeover Dou's strength swelled to more than a hundred thousand men holding the prefectures of Hebei; in AD 618 he sent an envoy with a memorial declaring himself a subject and was invested as Prince of Xia, and he later proclaimed himself emperor and built up a separatist regime rooted in Hebei. In December AD 621 the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, broke the Xia army in mass at the Ming River, and Dou Jiande was captured by his own men, taken to Chang'an and executed; the prefectures of Hebei then came over to the Tang in turn, and Hebei returned to the territory of the central dynasty. Looking back, the takeover on the southern Hebei plain in AD 617, which no detailed battle record preserves, was the first step of that ending: first the absorption of Wei Dao'er and Zhang Jincheng and the mastery of Hebei alone, then the uprooting of the whole thing by a Tang army in one set-piece battle — two things less than five years apart, with the battle of the Ming River between them.
